LESSON: TRANSPORT IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities in Eastern
Topic 3.4: Transport in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Transport in Eastern Africa, part of Resources and Economic Activities in Eastern in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need transport networks in our country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

A. identify the main transport networks in Eastern Africa on a map, Learner is guided to:  locate the main transport networks in Eastern Africa on a map Africa (road, railway, air and wate

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Transport in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: Learners engage with a Game Ranger confidently on possible solutions to the challenges facing tourism in

Eastern Africa.

● Citizenship: Learners demonstrate interest with interaction with others as they brainstorm, in groups, factors that promote

tourism in Eastern Africa.

Values:
● Unity: Learners collaborate with others as they discuss and formulate solutions to problems facing tourism in Eastern Africa.

● Patriotism: Learners proactively solve problems as they develop charts on challenges and solutions facing tourism in Eastern

Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Decision making skills: Learners participate in conservation of wildlife walk/run.

● Safety and Security: Learners observe precautionary measures as they visit a nearby tourist attraction site and write a report.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Learners use Creative Arts skills to draw a map of Eastern Africa and locate game reserves and national parks.

● Learners apply Religious studies knowledge as they participate in conservation of wildlife walk/run activities within the

locality.
